content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary of review (Rule LD — liquidated damages payable by Customer):**

- **Responsive locations checked:** Section 3 (Fees; Payment — p0018–p0022), Section 4 (Term; Termination; Termination Payment — p0023–p0029), Section 1.6 (our right to terminate "without penalty"), plus full-document searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "damages", "shall pay", "minimum fee". Only one Customer-payable liquidated amount exists.
- **Classification: deviation (walk-away territory).** Section 4.2(a) makes the Company pay HDI 50% of the trailing twelve months' Net Sales above $800,000 on *any* Company termination, payable in eight quarterly installments. Against fees of 30% of monthly Net Sales over $11,000, three months' fees are ~7.5% of annual Net Sales — the Termination Payment is many multiples of the fallback cap and can exceed the remaining contract value; it also bites even where we terminate for HDI's failure (only the narrow late-launch carve-out in §1.6 is protected).
- **Not flagged:** §1.6 ("terminate this Agreement without penalty") and §4.2(b) HDI-side wording, which benefit us.
- **Redline (preferred level, one surgical replace, minimality gate ok:true):** the formula in 4.2(a) is replaced with an unconditional statement that no termination payment, liquidated damages or penalty of any kind is payable by the Company; the comment offers the fallback of an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
